summary.intent: Assess Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness) readiness, clean up stale/drifted todos across Phase 70-73, then plan, execute, and ship Phase 72 — interrupted midway by a production CI fire (desktop-e2e and web-e2e regressions) that had to be diagnosed and fixed first.
summary.outcome: Fixed and merged two regression PRs (#601 FUSE seq-equivocation + D-16 driver fix + greptile perf opt; #600 web floor-store fix + sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency fix + 4 web-e2e flake source-fixes), all validated green in CI. Resumed and completed Phase 72 planning (research, pattern-mapping, 10-plan wave structure, plan-checker pass) and executed through Wave 5 of 6 (7/10 plans landed, SC#1-#6 mostly implemented), with a new SC#7-equivalent hardening plan (72-11) added mid-execution to fix vitest-v3 Mock-type drift across test files and wire test-inclusive typecheck into CI.

repo: gsd todos are retired by deletion from pending/ (moved to completed/ via git mv), not left in place — Phase 71 shipped without doing this, causing 8 stale todos

ci-e2e.yml (bundles Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — must dispatch manually with `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (not `-f ref=`, which 422s on older workflow definitions) to get pre-merge runtime validation

Playwright web-e2e ciFloor() only raises wait timeouts to 60s under CI (process.env.CI); local runs use the raw (often 15-30s) timeout, causing IPNS-gated-mutation tests (batch delete/move, folder create) to flake locally even though they pass in CI — CI=1 locally conflicts with webServer.reuseExistingServer (`!process.env.CI`) and requires a temporary config patch to test the true CI regime

pnpm typecheck in CI only runs each package's tsconfig.build.json (which excludes test files) plus tsconfig.scripts.json — test files are never typechecked in CI, hiding a systematic vitest v2→v3 Mock<> generic-typing drift (~63 errors across api-client/sdk-core/sdk)

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with three separate pieces of test/fixture drift never updated: desktop-e2e .mts driver using pre-rename share DTO field names (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName), sdk-e2e Test 21 assertion not accounting for its own same-CID idempotency, and it exposed a real FUSE seq=1 equivocation bug against its own new anti-equivocation gate
local API server can reject TEST_LOGIN_SECRET if running from a stale dist build — restart from source to fix
GSD phase-72 executor sandbox cannot read .env, so any task needing secret-gated sdk-e2e live runs must be deferred to the orchestrator/wave-gate level, not done inside the executor subagent

hooks JSON for plan:pre gates (research/pattern-mapper/tdd/schema-gate fragments) contains raw multiline strings that break both --raw and naive JSON parsing; requires a lenient custom parser that escapes control chars only inside string literals

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty'; a stale/dropped UploadComplete retry re-seals at seq=1 with a new CID, tripping the Phase 71 anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS before first-publish and routing Found outcomes into the existing CAS retry path instead of skipping.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (greptile P2 perf fix) to avoid a redundant second IPNS resolve when the caller already resolved the sequence via the equivocation guard; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after conflict.

readDurableFloors/writeDurableSeqFloor were still targeting retired IndexedDB stores (generation-high-water/seq-high-water) after Phase 70.1 collapsed them into a single rotation-floor store (DB cipherbox-rotation-state v2, keyed by nodeId) — test helper never updated, causing a deterministic failure.

getWriteBodyParams (and its bin/index.ts twin) previously fail-open on a transient IPNS resolve miss when a real writeKey is present, silently sealing an empty write-body and discarding the folder's write chain; Phase 72 plan 72-04 made both throw instead, preserving the legitimate zero-writeKey read-only fallback.

deleteItem previously filtered WriteChildRef by ipnsName instead of resolving the node's UUID via resolvePublishedNode, and updateFolderMetadataAndPublish's CAS-merge was a naive union that could resurrect a just-deleted WriteChildRef under a concurrent write; Phase 72 plan 72-03 fixed both (UUID-based resolve + base-aware merge/prune with a resurrection-guard test).

workflow: When a background/local reproduction run keeps hitting different flaky tests each retry, the reliable diagnostic is to run under the CI-equivalent timeout regime (e.g. CI=1) rather than repeatedly patching individual timeout values whack-a-mole style

Capture newly-discovered, in-scope-adjacent tech debt (e.g. CI typecheck gap) as a durable todo file immediately, then sequence it as the LAST plan in the current phase so it also covers work the phase itself is about to add

When a subagent-driven wave execution touches a shared hot file (client.ts) across many plans, serialize those plans even if the plan-index marked them parallel-safe, to avoid textual/semantic conflicts
Prefer sequential execution on the main tree over git worktree isolation for pnpm monorepos, since fresh worktrees lack node_modules and hit known failure modes
Dispatch e2e workflows that don't run on PRs manually against the fix branch before merging, rather than merging blind and trusting the post-merge run

friction: gh workflow run -f ref=... returned HTTP 422 because the target workflow definition predated that input; had to use --ref <branch> instead

Local Playwright runs repeatedly hit a moving target of flaky tests (4.10 batch delete → 4.11 batch move → 2.1 folder create) each blocking the downstream tests actually under verification, requiring 7 sequential background runs and a temporary playwright.config.ts patch to reach a definitive CI-equivalent pass
git commit hung ~2 minutes on a 1Password SSH signing prompt (known recurring issue) during the 72-01 executor run
Initial cat-file check on HEAD tree contents gave a false negative (said completed/ todo copies were missing when they were actually present), requiring a second decisive check to reconcile
hooks JSON for plan:pre fragments couldn't be parsed by --raw or standard JSON.parse due to raw multiline control characters in string values; had to write a custom lenient parser script twice

AskUserQuestion was answered ambiguously by the user ('is there anything that needs to be clarified...') rather than picking an option, requiring a follow-up read-through of all 9 todos before re-presenting the question
